gap: No result ChatGPT got states a current price for any model. BLUETTI's US store sells the Elite 30 V2, rated 600 W AC, for $289.99 (read 2026-11-13). That is the same price as Jackery's 300 W Explorer 300 ($289) and inside ChatGPT's own $270–300 estimate for the 600 W RIVER 3 Plus. Jackery's store lists the Explorer 300 v2 that ChatGPT carded as sold out.
standout_why: I opened four ranking pages. agentretrievalindex.com (compact-class comparison) gives no prices, only 'Check price on Amazon' links. testedwatts.com (2026-09-23) lists no prices and no measurements and uses datasheet specs only. powerbencher.com (300 W stories) lists no prices and says it did not test the units. None of these three notes that the Jackery Explorer 300 v2 is sold out at Jackery or that the BLUETTI AC2A is discontinued. Prices set against AC wattage are new and useful. They don't decide the pick alone, because I could not get today's maker prices for the RIVER 3 Plus or the Anker C300X.
decides: The pick stays at a 600 W unit, but there are now two 600 W choices at about $290: the RIVER 3 Plus (ChatGPT's pick, maker price not verified) and the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 at $289.99 on BLUETTI's store, a model we list. Both 300 W Jackery cards lose at this price: the Explorer 300 v2 is sold out at Jackery, and the Explorer 300 costs $289 for half the rated AC output. Below $150, the ALLPOWERS VOLIX P300 at $139 (300 W, 256 Wh) is the cheapest in-stock maker-store option. The Tenergy T320 ($225.99) loses on its 200 W AC limit.
